title: spec review: next_wave decision point v3: one execute_children_resolved predicate for next_wave, closable, build_ctx and routine_close; launches-counted per-goal cap that auto-clears; unfiled_labels None = unknown; strict wave-line regex
spec:
Goal T-1403, plan label E12v3 (respec of T-1469 after spec reviews T-1462 and T-1480 request_changes; every risk is answered
below). Wave 1 of T-1403 finished 2026-10-01 09:30 and nothing happened for 8.5 h: no decision point covers
'filed work done, plan has more waves'.

Facts (goal/T-1403 after E9 T-1439; locate by symbol): planner_runs.decision_points() yields scouts_done, held and
closable only; closable needs every execute child merged_into, so a goal with superseded execute children never
closes (T-1403 has T-1405, T-1410, T-1413, T-1414 superseded). tick() routes each point through build_ctx() and
decision.route() (unknown kinds -> escalate 'unknown:kind'), then run_group(); run() and run_group() skip when
_session_attached(). daemon calls planner_runs.reconcile()/tick() only when [planner].autonomous is true (live
pool.toml false; harness forces false): leave that gate. _claim's decision_requested map and _condition_resolved()
are per kind; every non-'held' kind is goal-keyed in _decision_task, _observed_outcome, reconcile/jev and the
closable-only branches of build_ctx and tick (gate_state unknown, routine). planner_packet._KIND_FALLBACK maps
kinds to decision types; a missing entry falls to 'other'. Plan text lives in STATE/plan.md: section
'## GOAL <goal id> ...' up to the next '## ' line; wave lines start with 'Wave <n>'; additions are bullets
'- E3 (wave 3, ...) ...'. Filed children carry constraints.plan_label.

Change:
1. planner_runs.unfiled_labels(goal_id, children) -> sorted list. Labels = tokens matching
   (?<![\w./:-])[A-Z]\d{1,2}[a-z]?(?:v\d+)?(?![\w/:-]) on wave lines (^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?Wave \d+\b) of the goal's
   section, plus the leading label of bullets ^\s*[-*]\s*<label>\s*\(wave \d+. Minus labels on lines starting
   'Dropped:' in that section. A label is filed when a child's plan_label equals it, or equals it followed by a
   lowercase letter or v<digits> (E11 -> E11a, A1 -> A1v2; A10 does NOT file A1). Fail safe (T-1462 #5): no
   plan.md, no section, OSError or UnicodeDecodeError -> []. Only the goal's section is read; the read happens
   only inside decision_points() for goals whose execute children are all merged_into or superseded (so the
   per-tick cost is zero for goals with queued/running work, T-1462 #6). Plan text is data: it yields only label
   tokens and never reaches a prompt except as those tokens.
2. decision_points(): for a goal with execute children where every execute child is merged_into or status
   'superseded', no child of any role is queued or running, no execute child is held, and unfiled_labels is
   non-empty -> yield (goal_id, 'next_wave', f"{goal_id}:{sha256(','.join(labels))[:12]}") unless _blocked; do not
   yield closable for that goal. CLOSABLE GAP DECIDED (T-1462 #2): closable now counts superseded execute children
   as resolved (every execute child merged_into OR superseded, same predicate as next_wave); with no unfiled
   labels a goal with superseded children becomes closable. Keep every existing closable test green by reading
   them first; test_closable_requires_every_execute_child_merged must still fail closable for a queued/held/done-
   unmerged child (only 'superseded' is newly accepted; adjust its fixture if it used superseded as the blocker).
3. next_wave in the goal-keyed paths (T-1462 #4): _decision_task returns the goal; _observed_outcome returns None
   for next_wave; tick() skips the closable-only gate_state/routine branches for next_wave; _record_running copies
   the point as [goal_id, payload_key] like closable. build_ctx: add unfiled_labels and goal_complexity.
   _claim decision_requested: 'file the next wave from plan.md'. _condition_resolved for next_wave: goal done, or
   the goal's current unfiled set hashes to a different key than the record's payload_key.
4. Retry and dedup (T-1462 #3): next_wave launches are capped PER GOAL across every payload_key: [planner].next_wave_max_launches (default 3, read with .get) bounds the number of next_wave decision runs launched for one goal (sum of attempts over the goal's next_wave records). At the cap, tick() launches nothing, notifies exactly once ('next_wave: Planner launched N times for <goal> without filing; edit plan.md, add a Dropped: line, or clear next_wave_capped') and writes next_wave_capped=true on the goal's newest next_wave record; a label-set change does NOT reset the cap, only clearing that field does. Each distinct key still follows the existing attempts/gave_up rule of _claim/reconcile.
5. decision.route(): kind next_wave -> required field unfiled_labels checked by key presence (an empty list is
   valid, T-1462 #6): missing -> escalate 'unknown:unfiled_labels'; empty -> none 'no_unfiled_work'; else escalate
   'next_wave_unfiled' (planner_router picks the tier). Add unfiled_labels to the evidence fields.
6. planner_packet._KIND_FALLBACK gains next_wave -> 'other' explicitly, with a comment, and the packet includes
   unfiled_labels in the goal section so the decision Planner reads them (planner_packet.py joins scope, T-1462
   #4, #7).
7. .orchestrator/prompts/planner-decision.md: one sentence: a next_wave decision means every filed execute task of
   the goal is merged or superseded while plan.md still lists unfiled labels; file the next wave from plan.md (SPEC
   RULE, depends_on by plan label) or record under 'Needs the human' why not, and list labels that will never be
   filed on a 'Dropped:' line.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_closable_requires_every_execute_child_merged
and test_decision_points_scouts_done_held_closable write no plan.md and must pass (adjust only as rule 2 says);
tests/test_decision.py::test_disabled_routes_everything_to_escalate and the unknown-field table must pass
unchanged; tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py: next_wave classifies as decision_type 'other' (do not edit
planner_taxonomy.py); tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py and tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py must pass.

Depends on E9 (merged). The human decides when [planner].autonomous goes true. Rollback (T-1462 #8): `git revert`
of the merge commit; existing next_wave records stay inert because decision_points() no longer yields the kind;
the Planner records it in decisions.md at merge.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by the line numbers quoted here.

v3 AMENDMENTS (answer spec review T-1480; each overrides the rule above where they differ):
E1. ONE resolution predicate: planner_runs.execute_children_resolved(children) -> bool (every execute child merged_into OR
    status 'superseded'). decision_points (next_wave and closable), build_ctx's all_children_merged for the closable kind,
    and routine_close's guard ALL call it, so a goal with merged plus superseded execute children and no unfiled labels
    routes closable end to end (test it through tick() with the launcher patched).
E2. next_wave_capped auto-clears when the goal's unfiled label set strictly shrinks (a label filed or Dropped) or a new
    execute child of the goal is created; no manual edit is required. The notification names that rule. Test: cap reached,
    then one label filed -> the flag clears and one launch happens.
E3. The cap counts LAUNCHES: _record_running appends to the record's launches list (it exists for the other kinds; if not,
    add 'launches': [ts, ...]); [planner].next_wave_max_launches compares against sum(len(launches)) over the goal's
    next_wave records, never against attempts. The check runs inside the claim lock in _claim so count and launch are atomic.
E4. unfiled_labels(goal_id, children) -> list | None: [] when plan.md is missing or has no section for the goal (nothing to
    file); None when the file exists but cannot be read or decoded (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) = unknown. decision_points:
    None -> no next_wave point and closable behaves as if there were no unfiled labels (today's behaviour). _condition_resolved
    for next_wave: None -> NOT resolved (the record stays as it is). Test the running-record case: a running next_wave
    record plus an unreadable plan.md is neither resolved nor relaunched.
E5. Wave lines are only lines matching ^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?Wave \d+\s*[:(] (a colon or an opening parenthesis right after the
    number). 'Wave 2 depends on E9 (merged)' is prose and yields no labels; test it alongside the path-like token case.
E6. The tick acceptance tests exercise the routes-configured path ([planner.routes].enabled true, as the harness pool.toml
    has it). The legacy branch of tick() ('routes' not in config, run() on the first point) is out of scope and documented
    as such in the planner_runs module docstring.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_next_wave_point_when_filed_work_resolved_and_plan_lists_unfiled_labels: passes: with STATE/plan.md holding a '## GOAL <id>' section whose wave lines name A1, A2, B1 and children plan_label A1 (merged) and A2 (superseded), decision_points() yields (goal, 'next_wave', key) and not closable; nothing is yielded while any child is queued/running or an execute child is held, or once B1 is filed (or listed on a 'Dropped:' line); a goal whose execute children are all merged or superseded with no unfiled labels yields closable; tick() records a skip and launches nothing while _session_attached() is true, and launches exactly one decision run for a next_wave point with route escalate when detached (launcher patched)

tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_unfiled_labels_fails_safe_and_matches_suffixes: passes: unfiled_labels returns [] with no plan.md or no goal section and None for an unreadable file (OSError patched) or a non-UTF-8 file; 'Wave 2 depends on E9 (merged)' yields no labels; a wave line whose prose contains 'B1' only inside a path-like or word token is not a label; 'Dropped: B9' removes B9; E11 is filed by plan_label E11a and A1 by A1v2 but A1 is not filed by A10; after [planner].next_wave_max_launches launches without filing, tick() notifies once and launches nothing until the record is cleared

tests/test_decision.py::test_next_wave_routes_escalate_or_none: passes: decision.route on kind next_wave returns escalate 'next_wave_unfiled' with unfiled_labels in the evidence when the list is non-empty, none 'no_unfiled_work' when the list is present but empty, and escalate 'unknown:unfiled_labels' when the field is missing
tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_next_wave_packet_lists_unfiled_labels: passes: the packet for a next_wave point maps to decision type 'other' and its goal section lists the unfiled labels

tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_closable_counts_superseded_children_end_to_end_and_cap_counts_launches: passes: a goal whose execute children are merged plus superseded with no unfiled labels is yielded as closable, build_ctx reports all_children_merged True and routine_close does not refuse it; with next_wave_max_launches 2 the third tick launches nothing, notifies once and sets next_wave_capped; filing one of the labels clears the flag and the next tick launches exactly once; a running next_wave record with an unreadable plan.md is neither resolved nor relaunched

risks.issue: Label extraction on wave lines also matches labels that are only referenced, e.g. 'Wave 3 (after E9, H6 ...)'. Those labels are never filed as children, so they count as permanently unfiled. The goal would then loop on next_wave until the launch cap and never close. 'Dropped:' is the only escape.

Counting superseded execute children as resolved lets a goal with only superseded children, and no merged one, become closable. Closing with nothing merged is wrong. A superseded child whose replacement was never filed is also treated as done.

E2 auto-clear needs state that the spec never defines: the label set (or count) at cap time, and the execute-child count at cap time. Without a stored field on the next_wave record, 'strictly shrinks' and 'new execute child' cannot be evaluated. Rule 4 says a label-set change does not reset the cap, E2 says it does if the set shrinks, and the two must be reconciled in one place.

Rule 4 (sum of attempts) and E3 (sum of launches) conflict, and rules 1 and 4 conflict with E4 and E5. The amendments override, but the implementer has to merge four layers of text. The launch cap check and the notify-once and next_wave_capped write sit in _claim under the lock, so the notification must not be sent while holding the lock. The notify-once flag must be written before or after, atomically.

The spec says routine_close and build_ctx 'all call' execute_children_resolved, but gives no insertion point for routine_close. If it lives outside the scope list (a routine or decision module), the change is out of scope. Locate it and either add it to scope or confirm that it is in planner_runs.py.

The adjacent tests that must pass unchanged are outside scope: test_planner_taxonomy.py, test_planner_runs_routing.py and test_planner_packet.py (the spec lists test_planner_runs_packets.py). Adding a kind to the route table or evidence fields may break the 'unknown-field table' test. The implementer cannot edit those tests, so the spec should say to run them explicitly in the focused set.

Acceptance bullets are compound: one test id asserts about 10 behaviours (queued, running, held, Dropped, superseded, attached session, launcher patch). A failure is hard to localise, and the same behaviours are covered across three test ids. Split them or list sub-assertions explicitly.

depends_on lists T-1439 while the body says 'Depends on E9 (merged)', and the packet base differs from goal/T-1403. Confirm that T-1439 is merged into the base, otherwise the symbols named (_condition_resolved, decision_requested map) may not exist yet.

suggested_spec_changes: Restrict label extraction to labels that are being introduced: bullets of the form '- <label> (wave N', or the first label on a 'Wave N:' line, or labels after an explicit 'files'/'adds' keyword. Alternatively, ignore labels that appear after 'after', 'depends', 'needs' or inside parentheses.
Require at least one merged execute child for execute_children_resolved to count as closable. An all-superseded goal should escalate instead.

Specify the record fields next_wave stores for E2: labels_at_cap (list) and execute_child_count_at_cap, plus the exact clear condition. Fold rules 4 and E3 into one rule that states the launches-based cap.
State that the cap notification is sent after the claim lock is released, and that next_wave_capped is written under the lock so notify-once is atomic.
Name the file and symbol where routine_close lives. Add it to scope if it is not in planner_runs.py.
Add the extra test files (test_planner_taxonomy.py, test_planner_runs_routing.py, test_planner_packet.py, test_decision.py) to the focused run list.
Add a test for a referenced-only label on a wave line (e.g. 'Wave 3 (after E9)'), covering the false-positive case.

Rewrite the spec as one consolidated version that incorporates the amendments, or add an explicit precedence table. The rollback note should also say that the closable change for superseded children is not inert after revert and must be reverted with the same commit.
